We need to propose a retrosynthesis route (max 3 steps) to target molecule: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We need leaves commercially available, total price <= $9999. Need to find suitable disconnections.

The molecule has a para-methyl phenyl sulfonamide attached to another phenyl ring bearing a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide (cinnamamide) attached to an aniline (anilide). So overall: p-tolyl-sulfonyl-phenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-phenyl-NH2? Wait the amide is C(=O)N attached to an aniline (c3ccccc3N). So it's a phenyl amide with an aniline substituent (anilide). So the target is a sulfonamide linking two phenyl rings, and one phenyl ring further attached to a cinnamamide with an aniline.

Potential retrosynthetic steps:

1. Disconnection of sulfonamide: could form via sulfonyl chloride (p-tolylsulfonyl chloride) reacting with an aniline (the phenyl bearing the cinnamamide). So step: p-tolylsulfonyl chloride + 4-aminophenyl-cinnamamide -> target.

Thus we need to have the aniline precursor: 4-(C=O)N-... Actually the phenyl bearing the sulfonamide also has the cinnamamide substituent at para? Let's examine SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Interpretation: Starting from tolyl ring (c1) with methyl at position 1, sulfonamide attached at position 4 (para). The sulfonyl group attached to another phenyl ring (c2) which has the cinnamamide substituent at para relative to sulfonyl? The SMILES: NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So sulfonamide nitrogen attached to sulfonyl attached to phenyl (c2). That phenyl has a para substituent /C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N (trans-cinnamamide with an aniline). So the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to sulfonyl, not to the phenyl. So the sulfonyl chloride would be p-tolylsulfonyl chloride (CH3-Ph-SO2Cl). Reaction with the aniline (the phenyl with cinnamamide) yields sulfonamide.

Thus step 1: coupling of sulfonyl chloride with aniline.

Now we need to get the aniline precursor: 4-(cinnamoyl)aniline? Actually the phenyl ring (c2) has the cinnamamide attached via carbon chain: /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH2 (aniline). So the phenyl ring is attached to the amide carbonyl via the double bond chain. So the aniline is at the end of the amide: Nc3ccccc3N (an aniline). So the amide is attached to the phenyl ring (c2) via the carbonyl carbon, and the amide nitrogen is attached to an aniline (c3). So the aniline is a separate phenyl ring with an NH2 substituent (para? Actually the SMILES: Nc3ccccc3N indicates an aniline with an NH attached to carbonyl (amide) and also an NH2 on the ring? Wait "Nc3ccccc3N" means N attached to carbonyl (amide) is attached to aromatic carbon (c3) which has an N substituent (the first N is the amide N, the second N is an aniline NH2 attached to the ring). So the aniline ring has an NH2 at the position where the amide attaches? Actually the SMILES: C(=O)N c3ccccc3 N . The N after carbonyl is attached to aromatic carbon (c3). Then that aromatic carbon also has an N substituent (the trailing N). So it's a phenyl ring with an amide attached at one position and an amino group at another (maybe ortho). But the SMILES "Nc3ccccc3N" indicates an aniline with two nitrogens: one attached to carbonyl (amide) and one free NH2 on the ring (para to each other? Not sure). So the product is a bis-aniline? This is complex.

Nevertheless, we can consider disconnection of the amide: the amide could be formed via coupling of an acid (cinnamic acid) with an aniline (the aniline ring). So step 2: cinnamic acid (or its activated derivative) + 4-aminophenyl (or appropriate) to give the amide.

But the cinnamic acid is attached to the phenyl ring (c2) via the double bond chain: /C=C/C(=O)N-... So the acid is trans-cinnamic acid (phenyl-CH=CH-COOH). The phenyl part is the same as the phenyl ring c2? Wait the cinnamic acid's phenyl is the same as the phenyl ring c2? Actually the SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the phenyl ring c2 has the cinnamoyl substituent attached via the double bond chain to the carbonyl, which then attaches to an aniline. So the phenyl ring c2 is the aromatic ring bearing the cinnamoyl group. So the cinnamic acid's phenyl is that same ring. So the amide formation is between the carboxylic acid of cinnamic acid and the aniline (c3). So we need cinnamic acid (or derivative) and aniline (c3) to form the amide.

Thus retrosynthesis:

Target -> disconnection 1: sulfonamide formation (p-tolylsulfonyl chloride + aniline precursor (phenyl with cinnamoyl amide)).

Aniline precursor: 4-(cinnamoyl)aniline? Actually the phenyl ring c2 has the cinnamoyl attached at para position relative to sulfonyl? The sulfonyl attaches to the nitrogen, not to the phenyl. So the phenyl ring c2 is attached to sulfonyl via S=O2-N? Wait sulfonamide: NS(=O)(=O)c2... So the nitrogen of sulfonamide is attached to the tolyl ring (via N) and to the sulfonyl group, which is attached to phenyl c2. So the phenyl c2 is attached to the sulfonyl group (SO2). So the phenyl c2 is the sulfonyl aryl group. That phenyl also has the cinnamoyl substituent. So the aniline precursor is the phenyl sulfonyl aryl (c2) with the cinnamoyl substituent and a free NH2? Wait the sulfonyl aryl is attached to sulfonyl, not to nitrogen. The sulfonyl group attaches to the phenyl via S=O2-Ph. So the phenyl c2 is not an aniline; it is just a phenyl ring bearing the cinnamoyl group. The sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the tolyl ring (p-tolyl) and to the sulfonyl group. So the sulfonyl chloride is p-tolylsulfonyl chloride (CH3-Ph-SO2Cl). Reaction with the phenyl ring c2 (which has a free amine? Actually the phenyl c2 does not have an amine; the sulfonyl chloride reacts with an amine (the tolyl sulfonamide nitrogen). Wait typical sulfonamide formation: sulfonyl chloride + amine -> sulfonamide. Here the amine is the tolyl sulfonamide nitrogen? Actually the nitrogen is attached to the tolyl ring (as part of an aniline). The tolyl ring has an NH attached to sulfonyl group. So the amine is p-toluidine (p-methyl aniline). So the sulfonyl chloride is the aryl sulfonyl chloride derived from the other phenyl (c2) with the cinnamoyl substituent. So we need aryl sulfonyl chloride: 4-(cinnamoyl)phenylsulfonyl chloride (i.e., 4-(cinnamoyl)benzenesulfonyl chloride). Then react with p-toluidine to give target.

Thus step 1: p-toluidine + 4-(cinnamoyl)benzenesulfonyl chloride -> target.

Now we need to get 4-(cinnamoyl)benzenesulfonyl chloride. This can be made from 4-(cinnamoyl)benzenesulfonic acid (or sulfonic acid) via chlorination (SO2Cl). The sulfonic acid can be obtained from sulfonation of 4-(cinnamoyl)benzene (i.e., 4-cinnamyl phenyl) with SO3. But maybe easier: start from 4-bromobenzene sulfonyl chloride? Not.

Alternative route: start from 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride (commercial) and then do Suzuki coupling to install the cinnamoyl phenyl? But the cinnamoyl is attached via a double bond chain, not directly phenyl. Actually the cinnamoyl substituent is a trans-CH=CH-CO- attached to the phenyl ring. So we could start from 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride, then do Heck coupling with cinnamic acid derivative? Or we could start from 4-iodobenzenesulfonyl chloride and do Heck with acrylate then convert to acid then amide.

But we have only 3 steps total. So we need a concise route.

Maybe we can consider disconnection of the C=C double bond: use Heck coupling of 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride with acrylamide? Actually we need the cinnamoyl attached to phenyl, then amide with aniline. Could do two steps: (1) Heck coupling of 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride with acrylamide (C=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2) to give the cinnamoyl sulfonyl chloride? Wait the product of Heck would be phenyl-SO2-Cl attached to CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2. That matches the target after sulfonamide formation with p-toluidine? Actually the target has sulfonyl attached to phenyl (c2) which has the cinnamoyl chain attached. So if we start from 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride, do Heck with acrylamide (CH2=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2) to give 4-(CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2)benzenesulfonyl chloride. Then react with p-toluidine to give final product. That's two steps.

Now we need to ensure the acrylamide (CH2=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2) is commercially available. Let's check: maybe "cinnamamide" (trans-cinnamamide) is commercially available. But we need the aniline attached to the amide nitrogen (i.e., N-phenylcinnamamide). Actually the amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl (c3) which also has an NH2 substituent. So the amide is N-(4-aminophenyl)acrylamide? Wait "Nc3ccccc3N" indicates the amide nitrogen attached to phenyl which also has an NH2 substituent (maybe at para). So the amide is N-(4-aminophenyl)acrylamide (para-aminophenyl). So the acrylamide is "N-(4-aminophenyl)acrylamide". That is commercially available? Possibly "p-aminocinnamamide". Might be available.

Thus step 1: Heck coupling of 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride with N-(4-aminophenyl)acrylamide to give sulfonyl chloride with cinnamoyl chain.

Step 2: Sulfonamide formation with p-toluidine.

Thus total 2 steps, within limit.

Now we need to verify that the reagents are commercially available and total price < $9999. Likely yes.

We need to produce JSON route: root is target molecule, children reaction nodes.

We need template IDs for the reactions. We need to find appropriate templates for Heck coupling and sulfonamide formation.

We can search for templates for "C=C" formation (Heck) and "sulfonamide formation" (sulfonyl chloride + amine). Use search_template_catalog_by_criteria with functional groups formed: "C-C double bonds" maybe for Heck? Let's search.
